# Introduction

The books that I have chosen for my lab are The Art of Invisiblity by Kevin Mitnick, Sandworm by Andy Greenberg and The Web Application Hackers Handbook by Dafydd Stuttuard and Marcus Pinto. I chose these books by asking a friend for some books they've read recently all related to the same topic. These books are all related to cyber security. I will record the title, authors, publication year, genre, and ISBN for each book. I will create my HTML file and JSON file on Visual Studios and then import the data using R. I do not anticipate having too much trouble with this code because I completed a Full Stack Web Development bootcamp last spring so I have worked with both HTML and JSON files. However to import each into R I plan to use the readHTML() method from the RVest package and the fromJSON() method from the Jsonlite package to read the data into my R Markdown file and then I will compare the data after any potential reformatting that may be required.

```{r installing-necessary-packages}
library(jsonlite)
library(rvest)
library(dplyr)

#Loading HTML File, Creating a table from the element with the class name "table"
html_books <- read_html("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Renagade316/DATA607-Labs/refs/heads/main/Lab7-HTML_%26_JSON/Books.HTML") |>
  html_element("table.books") |>
  html_table()

#Changing Date Format
html_books <- html_books %>% 
  mutate(`Publication Date` = as.Date(`Publication Date`, format = "%m/%d/%Y"))

#Turning the ISBN's into numbers
html_books <- html_books %>% 
  mutate(ISBN = as.numeric(gsub("-", "", ISBN)))

#Turning the tibble into a data frame
html_books <- data.frame(html_books)

#Renaming publication date
html_books <- html_books %>% rename(`Publication Date` = Publication.Date)

#Loading JSON doc
json_books <- fromJSON("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Renagade316/DATA607-Labs/refs/heads/main/Lab7-HTML_%26_JSON/Books.JSON")

#Removing the row names
rownames(json_books) <- NULL

#Setting the Date to proper format
json_books <- json_books %>% 
  mutate(`Publication Date` = as.Date(`Publication Date`, format = "%m/%d/%Y"))

#Displaying data
html_books
json_books

#Checking if identical
all.equal(html_books, json_books)
```

# Conclusion

In conclusion to create these data sets I created an HTML and Json file in Visual Studio Code and then placed both files into the same directory at first (later used the raw URL) to load the raw data set into R. For HTML I used the RVest package and the read_HTML() method as mentioned. I did not realize however, realize that this loaded the whole HTML file into the data set, so from there I used the html_element() method to find the table whose class I named "table" and then used html_table() to create a tibble. For the JSON file I just used the jsonlite package and the fromJSON() method to load the data frame. Lastly I did some tidying to reformat both data frames and used the all.equal method, which returns true if two dataframes and identical and false if not, but returns the differences between them to troubleshoot the differences until they all.equal returned true. Ultimately my previous knowledge of both HTML and Json helped greatly and I did not have many challenges or difficulties.
